  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}

> This notebook optimizes the typesetting parameters that control hyphenation &
> justification. During this process, LaTeX parameters are kept "fussy" but bad
> page breaks are disregarded. A grid search over paragraph indentation widths
> and word-space stretch/shrink factors identifies settings that produce the
> most consistent word space. Results are saved as a package dataset, see
> `help(hj_proofs)`.



Begin by enumerating all parameter combinations to explore.


``` r
hj_params <- expand_grid(
  # consider distinct layout candidate text widths (nested table)
  layouts = layout_candidates |>
    arrange(error, desc(text_pct)) |>
    slice_min(error, by = text_width, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    list(),

  # consider a range of sensible wordspace settings (nested table)
  ws = expand_grid(
    ws_min = seq(11 / 6, 11 / 5, length.out = 3),
    ws_avg = seq(11 / 4, 11 / 3, length.out = 5),
    ws_max = seq(11 / 3, 11 / 2, length.out = 9)
  ) |>
    filter(ws_min < ws_avg, ws_avg < ws_max) |>
    transmute(
      ws = ws_avg / 2.94556,
      ws_stretch = (ws_max - ws_avg) / 1.47278,
      ws_shrink = (ws_avg - ws_min) / 0.98186
    ) |>
    list(),

  # consider a range of harmonious paragraph indentation lengths
  parindent = c(12, 15, 16, 18, 20),

  # fine-tune LaTeX hyphenation & justification settings
  pretolerance = 100, # lower to 0 to skip; increase to 200 to make sloppy
  tolerance = 200, # increase to 500 or 1000 to make sloppy
  hfuzz = 0, # increase to 1 to make sloppy
  emergencystretch = 0, # increase to 0.5 or 1 to make sloppy
  doublehyphendemerits = 1e5, # 1e4 is too sloppy; increase to 1e6 if needed
  hyphenate_responded = FALSE, # avoid

  # don't penalize bad page breaks while evaluating hyphenation & justification
  interlinepenalty = 0, clubpenalty = 0, widowpenalty = 0, brokenpenalty = 0
) |>
  filter(pretolerance < tolerance) |>
  unnest(layouts) |>
  unnest(ws)
```

Proof each set of parameters, exclude any with problems, and then extend
acceptable parameter sets to all layout options. For each layout candidate, keep
the set of parameters that minimizes RMSE.


``` r
# for each set of params, typeset a proof
hj_proofs <- map_typeset(hj_params)

# identify problem-free proofs
hj_proofs <- inner_join(
  by = "id",
  hj_proofs,
  map_dfr(hj_proofs$id, parse_tex_log) |>
    filter(exception_count == 0, overfull_count == 0, underfull_count == 0) |>
    mutate(hyphen_runs = map_dbl(id, count_hyphen_runs)) |>
    filter(hyphen_runs == 0) |>
    with(tibble(id, map_dfr(id, analyze_whitespace))) |>
    filter(word_space_min > 1)
)

# for each set of acceptable params, typeset proofs for every layout candidate
hj_proofs <- hj_proofs |>
  select(-any_of(setdiff(names(layout_candidates), "text_width"))) |>
  left_join(layout_candidates, by = "text_width", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  map_typeset()

# re-identify problem-free proofs
hj_proofs <- inner_join(
  by = "id",
  hj_proofs,
  map_dfr(hj_proofs$id, parse_tex_log) |>
    filter(exception_count == 0, overfull_count == 0, underfull_count == 0) |>
    mutate(hyphen_runs = map_dbl(id, count_hyphen_runs)) |>
    filter(hyphen_runs == 0) |>
    with(tibble(id, map_dfr(id, analyze_whitespace))) |>
    filter(word_space_min > 1)
)

# for each layout candidate, pick the set(s) of params with the lowest RMSE
hj_proofs <- hj_proofs |>
  slice_min(
    word_space_rmse,
    by = c("page_height", "page_width", "text_height_lines", "text_width"),
    n = 1
  )
```
